Change c0399. Location: 1818 Vol. III, Ch. IV; 1831 Ch. XXI.

Context before (unchanged): How can I describe my sensations on beholding it?

1818 text: I feel yet parched with horror, nor can I reflect on that terrible moment without shuddering and agony, that faintly reminds me of the anguish of the recognition. The trial, the presence of the magistrate and witnesses, passed like a dream from my memory, when I saw the lifeless form of Henry Clerval stretched before me.

1831 text: I feel yet parched with horror, nor can I reflect on that terrible moment without shuddering and agony. The examination, the presence of the magistrate and witnesses, passed like a dream from my memory, when I saw the lifeless form of Henry Clerval stretched before me.

Diff: I feel yet parched with horror, nor can I reflect on that terrible moment without shuddering and agony [-, that faintly reminds me of the anguish of the recognition-] . The [-trial-] {+examination+} , the presence of the magistrate and witnesses, passed like a dream from my memory, when I saw the lifeless form of Henry Clerval stretched before me.

Context after (unchanged): I gasped for breath; and, throwing myself on the body, I exclaimed, "Have my murderous machinations deprived you also, my dearest Henry, of life?

result.rationale: The main change is the deletion of "that faintly reminds me of the anguish of the recognition," which removes a retrospective link to the creature's recognition scene. "Trial" becomes "examination," a lighter legal term that reduces the sense of formal judicial proceedings.
